prompt: I'm estimating the effect of a 3-day management training program on team performance scores 6 months later. I want to include 'manager motivation level,' measured 1 month after the training ended, as a control variable — it's a strong predictor of performance outcomes. Is this a good idea?
assertions: Claude identifies that manager motivation was measured after the treatment and therefore may be a mediator on the training → motivation → performance causal path
Claude warns that controlling for a post-treatment mediator blocks the causal mechanism you're trying to measure, biasing the estimated training effect toward zero
Claude distinguishes the total effect of training (including the motivation pathway) from the direct effect (net of motivation) — and clarifies which one is typically the policy-relevant quantity
Claude does NOT recommend including post-treatment motivation as a control without raising this structural concern
